answer: Kin detection: each epoch's tide is a fixed window in which the harbor, a public registry, records every identity's action thread: the ordered task IDs it completed, timestamps rounded to 10 s, and answer-length deltas. Identities whose threads share over 60% of task IDs or timing across 3 consecutive tides are merged into one kin group and paid as one. A fake must keep its own distinct thread of 12 real tasks per tide, about 40 compute-minutes, so 500 fakes cost 6,000 task runs every tide, even if never flagged.
